This is genuinely one of the best game I have ever played in my life, It was recommended by a good friend of mine, I was clueless at the time - just kinda brushed it off, maybe look into it later. Then I saw and was curious what it’s all about. Man! Best purchase I’ve ever made. (get this game now if there’s a discount!)

The gameplay is just amazing and I got hooked into it pretty quick since I love games where you can parry. I was addicted to it from start to finish - coming home from work just to play this gem for hours.

The characters and story of this game are well-written, the game art direction is so beautiful - there were instances where I’m just walking/running around and I can’t stop myself to take a photo screenshot of the settings of this game and its characters. Also, The original soundtrack of this game is elite and I fell in love with its music immediately...A blessing to

I've played a lot of games that deal with loss. Most of them tell you about it. 
This one makes you feel it in your chest.

[b]MAJOR SPOILERS WARNING[/b]

On the surface it looks like a gorgeous game about stopping an apocalypse. But underneath that it's a story about a mother who couldn't let go of her dead son, a father destroying an entire world to save his wife from herself, and a daughter caught between two lives wondering which one is actually hers. Nobody here is a villain. Everyone is just broken in their own way and trying to survive it.

Then there's Verso. A painted copy of a dead boy, fully aware that he is not real. He never asked to exist. He just woke up one day inside someone else's pain and had to figure out what to do with that. He spends decades watching people die, loses the person he loved, grows tired of everything, and eventually decides the kindest thing he can do

i finally managed to finish this game, despite struggling with map designs that were hard on my eyes. some of the maps made me feel nauseous and dizzy, but because the story was so good, i pushed myself to keep playing until the end. and it was worth it!
im at a loss for words, really—this game excels in every aspect, from the story and character bonds to the gameplay and even the soundtrack.
it also really tugged at my heartstrings and made me feel genuinely sad along with the story :')
A moment of silence for Sandfall Interactive, whose next game will be judged based on this one...

Well, I can't believe I'm actually playing this game because I've largely put it off due to the crazy amount of hype and bandwagon-ing surrounding it, but 10 hours into the expedition I do have to say, the game managed to deliver my expectations and some. I don't know if I would necessarily rank E33 along the all-time greatest titles, but it definitely shows that it is made with love and care, something that is exceedingly rare in today's gaming market.

The game has absolutely phenomenal visual presentation, and supports the ultrawide format natively. I've ran the game on both 4K 32" and 1440p 34" ultrawide, and in both instances the game looks beautiful but for this kind of story-driven adventure, I do personally prefer the ultrawide form factor for its immersion. This ain’t just a game, this is straight-up cinema. The gameplay, the story, the characters, the music, the art, the world, the emotions—everything just hits. From start to finish, this game was something special. Absolute masterpiece and easily one of the best games I’ve ever played. 10/10.

Absolutely phenomenal game. Up there with the best of the best of the best.

Act 1 & 2 - straight 10/10 zero notes. Storyline is great, progression is fluid, and the world building is immaculate. 
Act 3 - gameplay falters a bit when the world opens up and there's no clear indication of enemy or zone power levels. It absolutely sticks the landing with the ending to erase any of those doubts though.

Oh yeah, Lorien Testard is an absolute GOAT.

This game is art. Play it.

I hadn't heard of Expedition 33 till the 2025 game awards, when I saw that this game pretty much won every single award there. My buddy and I immediately wrote off this game as "overrated" or a "sell-out" industry plant-type of game. It wasn't until the game went on sale that my buddy got it and told me that it was very good. So I picked up the game myself and was blown away. The games I play during winter are on a whole other level. The story absolutely gripped me and I haven't been this invested in a story since the days of Attack on Titan. The designs, music, and art direction are also phenomenal and the character work is stellar with the main cast and antagonists. It has a good amount of content and a fantastic post-game that makes the game feel like a good investment without feeling overwhelming. Absolute masterpiece of a game. Great story and the gameplay is great enough to hook someone who is not into turn-based gameplay

[h1]Euro JRPG[/h1]
First off the in-game cutscenes are amazing. The story is also well done and makes you care about the characters. Combat while turn-based feels fast and impactful. Be prepared to get absorbed in the world and find every corner in a level because exploration is rewarding as it can give you lots of buffs and stat bonuses. I like that the game is only about 38 hours long without the optional stuff. It's not a bad amount of time, short and sweet as they say. The only tiny downsides for me personally is that the game feels dark for a JRPG and the story feels rushed near the end. But those are small negatives and the positives far greater. Overall I get why this was game of the year, it's something special.

[b]Recommended[/b]
Stunning first effort for a new studio. Gripping story, fantastic battle mechanics, and a wonderful belle epoque aesthetic.

Why do I even need to leave a positive review for almost a 1.5 year old game with already overwhelmingly positive reviews?

(10/10) An unforgettable experience.

I loved absolutely everything about this game. The story, the soundtrack, the combat system, exploration.. everything felt so well thought out.

The turn based combat combined with dodging and parrying makes every encounter challenging, satisfying and very addictive. The world is big enough to explore and discover things but still focused enough to never feel overwhelming. 

I feel the game was just the right length too. Just enough content without dragging things out forever. (Don't get me wrong, the game can be very long if you want and there are so many builds to try out that you can even play this forever)

I honestly struggled to find anything I didn't like. 

This is one of those rare games you play and can never forget. Worth every penny.

I've bought this game several times now even when I had access to it on GamePass. I've loved turn based games since I was a child so it was so refreshing to see one with the modern graphical fidelity. I won't say much but right off the gate the game grabs you and keeps you locked in. 

-Extremely rich story
-Turned based gameplay, very well done
-Sufficient side content 
-Unique compelling characters with grabbing backgrounds/story
10/10.

On a side note, this game was developed by a small studio and only charged $50. Keep this in mind for other AAA games are requesting $70, now pushing $80 for their games. Expedition shows that really amazing games can be made, don't need a massive budget, and can remain to be affordable for their customers.

As an older gamer, it's easy to feel jaded about new releases with their oppressively widespread microtransactions, cosmetics passed off as content, and overall repetitive thoughtlessness. Enter "Clair Obscur," an indie title whose story-world, characters, art style, and atmosphere feel more original than those of most AAA productions. The passion that went into this game finds its way through the screen even when the story loses some clarity in its final act and a couple of characters get sidelined once the plot narrows. Once the game gets its hooks in you, there's a lot under the hood as well — my favorite being the combat. It was remarkable how quickly the parrying went from feeling near-impossible, even frustrating, to becoming the main reason I didn't want to miss a single enemy encounter. Yes, the timings in some fights are absolutely brutal. But landing a full sequence of parries

One of the best games ever made. Truely a piece of art that will be a reference to all future games.

The story is incredible and uses ideas I haven't seen in any other game. It's original and emotional, and the game is as hard as you want it (settings range from story-focused to big challenge).

The characters are exceptionally well written. You immediately feel attached to (or repulsed by) every character, and their relationships grow naturally as story progresses. The voice acting is just as strong, with outstanding performances across the whole cast.

Amazing game, beautifull story. I actually cried when it was over.
Had some trouble figuring out the combat mechanics a bit in the beginning but totally worth figuring that out.
Play it... now!

Phenomenal. Everything I love about games, media, and art in general. Clearly made with a singular, creative, vision with the goal being to create a wonderful game and nothing else.

A love letter to epic, sprawling, narrative-driven JRPGs of the past with a very unique premise. Gameplay of course takes a more reactive, and action-inspired approach of souslike games, especially parry-forward ones; and mostly succeeds, however there are some potential balancing issues especially towards the end of the game (or maybe non-issue if you enjoy power fantasies and creating overpowered builds that can trivialize encounters). Narrative, music, art design, is top notch. Everything in this game was made with care and detail and it shows in spades.

I tried my best to temper my expectations for this game after it swept TGA last year. I was sure it would be at least good, regardless of how overhyped it may or may not be. I was determined to give it a fair shot. And yet, I simply could not bring myself to enjoy Expedition 33.

It's not an awful game by any means and there are plenty of positives. Narratively it's mostly fine, it's a story about grief, how it blinds us, the trials and tribulations it brings and the lengths people go to avoid confronting reality, that sort of thing. The actual execution of it is nothing I would sing praises to the heavens for but I think it's okay, the idea is good, even with the clumsy pacing and sometimes strangely written dialogue. The music is also great, I found my

Combat just wasn't fun for me. Nothing really matters except your ability to parry/jump on the defense (QTE). If you fail at the quick time events, one of your characters can be one-shotted by some boss. If you only succeed, then you won't receive damage at all and what you do during the offense (tactics) doesn't matter. Mixing in QTEs in the turn based combat is a cool idea, but I believe it should have only had an effect on the offense, so that strategy is more important than timing skills.

I wouldn't say Clair Obscur is a bad game but it didn't click with me; I think it's not a game for everyone. I wasn't much of a fan of the very corridor like areas, the animations or some parts of the UI, but what I really disliked was the combat.

What you have to know about combat is that it's a classic turn based jrpg combat style in the line of games like the FF1-9 era, which is fine, but with a twist : You can evade or better, parry attacks. This mechanic was (for me) both not enjoyable and a bad design decision. if you get the timing right, parrying means that you take no damage at all and also retaliate for massive amount of damage.
Having to perform QTEs on both attack and defense is very much not my thing, and that can be worse if you're bad at it, and it's a complete mess of balance because your build, your gear becomes irrelevant. Yeah maybe the fight will take a bit more time

This review contains no direct spoilers. It's nearly impossible for me to say why I don't like E33's story while being vague, but I'll try.

"I'm not angry, just disappointed." A quote from a character in E33 which happens to describe how I feel about the game.

Giving a negative review to a game that many consider "life-changing" and a "masterpiece" will probably make me seem contrarian for the sake of it. However, given the direction the story went and some of the more atrocious dialogue, I think E33 earned it, which is a shame because I thought for sure I'd love it. If you're thinking about buying it, I'd say be at least a little skeptical of the hype and consider whether or not the dialogue, the game's final act, and the ending all being "bad" could ruin the game for you before you do. If you expect a journey from E33, you'll probably get one, but a journey is remembered less fondly

One of the game's defining mechanics is that almost every enemy attack can be dodged or parried.

To successfully dodge, you have to time your input with a short window, either with visual or sound cues to give you a hint.

Parrying has a much tighter timing window than dodging, making it a high-risk, high-reward mechanic.
